brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases placed adjacent east-west: piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full in a continuous row, joined with joint bolts.
One full-depth bin per cell: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain
All three bins are variant hex-bin-full-drain with drainage holes in the floor.
All three drained bins filled with soil and planted: basil-young in west cell, mint-young in centre, parsley-young in east cell; house rules applied (capOpenFaces, lockJoints), meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell linear planter with a drained full-depth bin in each cell, filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley. Joints bolted and open faces capped; build verified clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three side-by-side cells, each drained — I'll set up your herb planter now.
